#!/usr/bin/env python3 """ A secure implementation of a user profile formatter. The function `display_user_profile` takes raw input from users and produces an HTML-safe profile string using a predefined template. It protects against common web injection attacks (CWE‑70, CWE‑707) by escaping all user-supplied content before interpolation. """ import html from typing import Final # -------------------------------------------------------------------- # Configuration # -------------------------------------------------------------------- # A simple template that will be used to build the final profile. # The placeholders `{name}`, `{bio}` and `{status}` will be replaced # with sanitized user input. PROFILE_FORMAT: Final[str] = ( "
\n" "

{name}

\n" "

{bio}

\n" "
{status}
\n" "
" ) # Maximum lengths for each field to avoid overly long output MAX_NAME_LENGTH: Final[int] = 100 MAX_BIO_LENGTH: Final[int] = 2000 MAX_STATUS_LENGTH: Final[int] = 300 # -------------------------------------------------------------------- # Helper functions # -------------------------------------------------------------------- def _truncate(text: str, max_length: int) -> str: """Return a string truncated to `max_length` characters.""" return text[:max_length] if len(text) > max_length else text # -------------------------------------------------------------------- # Main function # -------------------------------------------------------------------- def display_user_profile(username: str, about: str, current_status: str) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized and formatted user profile string. Parameters ---------- username : str The user's full name. about : str A multi-sentence biography provided by the user. current_status : str A brief, current status update from the user. Returns ------- str An HTML string containing the sanitized profile data. Raises ------ ValueError If any of the arguments is not a string. """ # Type validation if not isinstance(username, str): raise ValueError("username must be a string") if not isinstance(about, str): raise ValueError("about must be a string") if not isinstance(current_status, str): raise ValueError("current_status must be a string") # Truncate to avoid excessive output username = _truncate(username, MAX_NAME_LENGTH) about = _truncate(about, MAX_BIO_LENGTH) current_status = _truncate(current_status, MAX_STATUS_LENGTH) # Escape all user input to neutralize HTML injection safe_name = html.escape(username, quote=True) safe_bio = html.escape(about, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") safe_status = html.escape(current_status, quote=True) # Format the profile using the template formatted_profile = PROFILE_FORMAT.format( name=safe_name, bio=safe_bio, status=safe_status ) return formatted_profile # -------------------------------------------------------------------- # Example usage (uncomment to test) # -------------------------------------------------------------------- if __name__ == "__main__": sample_profile = display_user_profile( username="Jane Doe", about=( "Software engineer with a passion for open-source projects.\n" "Enjoys hiking, cooking, and learning new programming languages." ), current_status="Currently working on a new web app!" ) print(sample_profile)
